Warka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Warka, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Warka grew significantly from the late 18th century, and the town later became seat of the Vurka Hasidic dynasty; by 1921, 2,176 Jews lived there before deportation to Warsaw in February 1941 and murder in 1942-1943. The cemetery's exact founding is unconfirmed, though it likely dates to the turn of the 19th century - it must have existed by 1848, when the dynasty's founding Rebbe, Izrael Icchak Kalisz, was buried there. Efforts to fence and enlarge the grounds began around 1850, with a final land purchase likely occurring in 1917. The cemetery probably remained active until Warka's Jews were deported in 1941. Around 1990, the Hasidic community built a red-brick ohel over the Rebbe's presumed grave, though today the site suffers from ongoing problems: littering, antisemitic graffiti on the ohel, and periodic erosion that causes buried remains to slide down the hillside.
